Use another taxonomic backbone

Source: R/backbone.R
WFO.backbone.Rd

Converts a taxonomic list (for example the World Checklist of Vascular Plants, or a list for another group of organisms) into a backbone that WFO.match(), WFO.one() and the other functions of this package can use instead of the World Flora Online.

Usage

WFO.backbone(
  x,
  taxonID = "taxonID",
  scientificName = "scientificName",
  scientificNameAuthorship = "scientificNameAuthorship",
  acceptedNameUsageID = NULL,
  taxonomicStatus = NULL
)

new.backbone(
  x,
  taxonID = "taxonID",
  scientificName = "scientificName",
  scientificNameAuthorship = "scientificNameAuthorship",
  acceptedNameUsageID = NULL,
  taxonomicStatus = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A data.frame with the taxonomic list.

taxonID

Name of the column with the identifiers of the names.

scientificName

Name of the column with the full names (without authors).

scientificNameAuthorship

Name of the column with the naming authors.

acceptedNameUsageID

Name of the column with, for synonyms, the identifier (taxonID) of the accepted name; empty for accepted names. If NULL, all names are treated as accepted.

taxonomicStatus

Name of the column with the status of the name (such as "Accepted" or "Synonym"). If NULL, names with an acceptedNameUsageID become "Synonym" and the others "Accepted".

Value

A data.table with the columns taxonID, scientificName, scientificNameAuthorship, acceptedNameUsageID and taxonomicStatus, followed by the other columns of x.

Details

All columns are converted to character. Other columns of x are kept. An acceptedNameUsageID that refers to the record itself is emptied (with a message), as is a missing one.

Names

WFO.backbone() is the name of this function from WorldFloraFast 1.0.3 on, in line with the other functions of the package. new.backbone(), its name in WorldFlora, remains available and gives the same results; its name resembles an S3 method new() for objects of class "backbone", which it is not.

References

Kindt, R. (2021). Standardizing mammal species names with the Mammal Diversity Database via WorldFlora. https://rpubs.com/Roeland-KINDT

Examples

x <- data.frame(
  id = c("A1", "A2", "A3"),
  name = c("Felis catus", "Felis domesticus", "Panthera leo"),
  author = c("Linnaeus, 1758", "Erxleben, 1777", "(Linnaeus, 1758)"),
  accepted = c("", "A1", "")
)
bb <- WFO.backbone(x,
  taxonID = "id", scientificName = "name",
  scientificNameAuthorship = "author", acceptedNameUsageID = "accepted"
)
m <- WFO.match("Felis domestica", WFO.data = bb, verbose = FALSE)
#> Checking for fuzzy matches for 1 records
#> 
#> Checking new accepted IDs
m[, c("spec.name", "scientificName", "Old.name")]
#>         spec.name scientificName         Old.name
#> 1 Felis domestica    Felis catus Felis domesticus
